title: PC 7 has no internet
instructions:
## A ticket from the school computer lab

You support a senior high school in Ho. The ICT teacher logs a ticket: one lab PC cannot reach the internet before a class at 10:00. Work the six-step method: identify the problem, form a theory, test it, plan and carry out the fix, verify, and document. Read the evidence before each choice.

nodes.title: Identify the problem
nodes.text: The ticket says only "internet not working on PC 7". What do you do first?

evidence.title: The ticket
evidence.text: From: Mr Agbeko, ICT teacher. "Internet not working on PC 7. Class at 10." Logged 08:40.

evidence.title: Two minutes with Mr Agbeko
evidence.text: The other 23 PCs work. PC 7 worked on Friday. Over the weekend the cleaners moved the desks to mop the floor. No one has installed anything.

choices.text: Ask what changed, check whether other PCs work, and try to reproduce the fault
choices.feedback: Correct. One PC failing, the rest fine, and desks moved at the weekend already points somewhere.

choices.text: Reinstall Windows to start from a clean state
choices.feedback: That is a fix without a diagnosis, and it destroys evidence and an hour.
Twenty-three other PCs are online, so the provider is not the problem.

nodes.title: Form a theory
nodes.text: You run ipconfig and ping on PC 7.

evidence.title: ipconfig and ping output
evidence.text:
Ethernet adapter: Media state . . . : Media connected
IPv4 Address . . : 169.254.37.12
Subnet Mask . . . : 255.255.0.0
Default Gateway . : (none)

ping 192.168.10.1 → Destination host unreachable.

choices.feedback: DNS only matters once the PC has an address and a gateway. This one has neither.

choices.text: The PC never got a DHCP lease (169.254 is a self-assigned address), so suspect the cable or the switch port it moved to
choices.feedback: Correct. A 169.254 address means the DHCP server was not reached. After desks were moved, the physical path is the first suspect.
The adapter reports "Media connected", so it sees a link. Test the cheaper causes first.

choices.text: Move PC 7's cable to the port PC 8 uses, which is known to work, and change nothing else
choices.feedback: Correct. Change one thing at a time against a known-good reference, so the result means something.

choices.text: Replace the cable, change the port, update the driver and reset the router at once
choices.feedback: If it starts working you will not know which change fixed it.
A firewall does not stop a DHCP lease from being issued.

nodes.title: Plan and fix
nodes.text: On PC 8's port, PC 7 gets 192.168.10.57 and browses. With PC 7's own cable on PC 8's port it fails again. What is the fix?

choices.text: Replace PC 7's patch cable, which was crushed under the moved desk, and route the new one away from the desk legs
choices.feedback: Correct. The cable is the one thing that failed in both tests.

choices.text: Leave PC 7 on PC 8's port permanently
choices.feedback: That moves the problem to PC 8.
The switch port worked with a good cable.

nodes.title: Verify and document
nodes.text: PC 7 is online again with a new cable. What closes the ticket properly?

choices.text: Have Mr Agbeko confirm it works, note the cause and fix in the ticket, and add a knowledge-base line about cables under desks after cleaning
choices.feedback: Correct. Confirmed by the user, documented for the next technician, and turned into prevention.
The next technician learns nothing, and the same fault will return after the next mopping.

choices.text: Leave the ticket open in case it breaks again
choices.feedback: Open tickets that are already resolved distort the queue and the service-level figures.

nodes.title: Ticket closed by 09:20
nodes.text: Root cause: a crushed patch cable after desks were moved. Fixed, verified with the user, documented, with a note to check cables after cleaning days.

hints: Ask what changed since it last worked.
An address starting 169.254 means the PC gave itself an address because no DHCP server answered.
Swap one thing for a known-good one and test again.

checks.label: You read the interview and the ipconfig output
At least four of the five decisions are right
checks.message: Fewer than four of the five were right. Read the feedback and run the case again.

realityNote: CompTIA A+ teaches this same six-step method. Most network faults in school labs turn out to be the physical layer: cables, ports and power.
